scope: Full municipal context baseline before the fire; forms and grades are reconstructed, not parcel-identification claims.

claims.label: reconstructed river banks

citations.citation: Chicago Board of Public Works. Tenth Annual Report to the Common Council, for the municipal year ending March 31, 1871. Chicago, 1871.
what_it_supplies: Bridge existence, construction years, reported lengths and March 31 traffic counts. Madison bridge is specified as all iron; others distinguish wooden or iron chords.
Contracted sidewalk work, park improvements and canal-opening chronology.
Wooden-block paving by street stretch (the warrants of 1870-71) and the city's wooden-block and boulder pavement by division, in lineal feet.
The city's fire hydrants: their number at March 31, 1871, and each of the year's 258 new ones by street corner.
what_it_does_not_supply: October 8 operating conditions, Sunday traffic volume, exact truss members, road widths or continuous pavement on every block.
Individual building footprints or facades.

citations.citation: S. Augustus Mitchell, Jr. Chicago. 1870. Approximately 1:31,000. University of Illinois Map and Geography Library; Wikimedia Commons surrogate.
what_it_supplies: Named streets and diagonals, river courses, lake edge, lakefront railroad and lagoon relationships, rail corridors and named parks.
Coverage from Fullerton Avenue to Thirty-first Street and Western Avenue to Lake Michigan.
what_it_does_not_supply: Individual building footprints, occupants, exact paving, engineered widths or elevations.
The western extension to Fortieth Avenue or southern continuation to Egan Avenue; these require separate evidence and reconstructed geometry.

citations.citation: A. Ruger. Chicago in 1868 from Schiller Street north side to 12th Street south side. Chicago Lithographing Co., 1868. Library of Congress 73693350.
what_it_supplies: Contemporary pictorial context: dense commercial buildings, low gabled dwellings, churches, warehouses, railway facilities and waterfront activity.
Central-city spatial relationships from Schiller Street to Twelfth Street.
what_it_does_not_supply: Surveyed footprints, accurate heights, calibrated roof pitches or unchanged October 1871 appearance for individual properties.
Photographic color or an exhaustive citywide building inventory.

notes: The 1870 map's river routes carry reconstructed channel widths bounded by period swing-bridge spans, with a broad bank transition at the context field resolution.

notes: No 1835 Lake Michigan stage record located. The mid-1830s fall in a high-water phase; 580 +/- 1.5 ft ASL is the working assumption. Check NOAA/GLERL historical Michigan-Huron reconstructions to narrow it.
Z = 0.0 ft at the summer-1835 lake and river water surface
